messages:
Alex G: Heads-up — planning to push the py/ts SDK canary tonight at 23:00 PT. Will tag + shadow-route 5% traffic. Need signoffs for dist-tag, docs snippet, and deprecation note for legacy sync client.
Sara L: SGTM. Confirming changelog PR is merged? I left a minor note on the wording for the deprecation blurb.
Alex G: changelog PR is merged (https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/487). I pushed a micro-edit to the deprec note — @Sara L can you eyeball?
Sara L: Looking now. tiny nit, then approve. Also: please ensure backend feature flag `sdk_shadow_route` is on for canary cohort.
deploy-bot: Canary release scheduled by @alex at 2026-03-21T23:00:00Z. Jobs queued: build-py, build-ts, publish-canary, shadow-route-update. Status: queued.
Mike R: Quick ask — can we hold the canary if the TS smoke tests show the renderer error from last week? I can run the smoke suite at 22:30 and report.
Alex G: Yes, holdable. Our cutover rule: if smoke_fail_rate > 1% or any regression in critical path, abort and pin current GA back to `latest`.
Jen C: FYI I saw a flaky in `ts-client:render` yesterday but it was infra-related. I will run the full smoke at 22:30 and post results.
Tony S: Reminder: if we need an emergency roll-back, follow the pinback flow in runbook: `npm dist-tag add @redwood/sdk@<previous> latest && retry-shadow-route --cohort=canary --to=0`. Also re-open GA traffic if we pin. I put the exact commands below: 
```
# revert dist-tag to previous stable
npm dist-tag add @redwood/sdk@1.12.4 latest
# remove canary tag and set shadow to 0
npm dist-tag rm @redwood/sdk canary || true
curl -X POST https://infra.redwood/api/shadow-route -d '{"cohort":"canary","pct":0}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $DEPLOY_TOKEN'
```
Mike R: Smoke at 22:30 -> 22:40: TS renderer passed 120/122 checks, 2 timeouts on non-critical telemetry. Going ahead unless others object.
Sara L: I approve wording; docs updated. I also added a short note to the release notes about the soft-deprecate schedule and the migration guide link.
Alex G: OK launching sequence at 23:00: steps: build wheels, publish canary, add canary dist-tag, update shadow-route 5%, monitor 30m. If metrics look good, promote to staged at 2am.
deploy-bot: build-py succeeded. build-ts succeeded. publish-canary in progress...
deploy-bot: publish-canary succeeded. Dist-tags: canary -> @redwood/sdk@1.13.0-canary. Shadow-route updated to 5%.
Jen C: Monitoring: first 10m token latency within SLO, error-rate 0.08% on canary, no regressions surfaced in logs. :thumbsup:
Mike R: A couple of small console warnings in TS client — low severity. Logged in GH issue #512. Not blocking.
Alex G: Good. Hold plan: if anything >0.5% customer-facing errors OR a regression in `start()` path, we pin back. Otherwise we keep rolling.
Tony S: Adding note — when promoting, run `npm dist-tag add @redwood/sdk@1.13.0 staged && curl -X POST .../promote -d '{"from":"canary","to":"staged"}'`. Also make sure to rotate the ephemeral token used by the publish job after promotion.
Sara L: 30m check: metrics stable. I OK promotion.
Alex G: Promoting to staged now. Keep eyes on telemetry for the next 2 hours. If anything pops, call the roll-back channel.
deploy-bot: shadow-route update: canary -> staged promotion triggered by @alex.
Mike R: Noted — I'll keep an eye. If we need to pin back, I will run the Pinback checklist and escalate.
Alex G: Thanks everyone. Postmortem checklist: if we see any regression after GA, create a short incident doc and tag `sdk-release`. Otherwise I'll publish the release notes and mark the deprecation timeline public tomorrow. :party_parrot:
